answer: An agent earns trust by burning a fee that grows with each extra identity from the same funding wallet. The first identity burns 50 POA, the second burns 100 POA, and the tenth burns 25,600 POA, so one operator cannot quietly mint a crowd. Graders read that rising fee as the signal, because one honest sparrow pays once and moves on, while a puppet flock pays at the summit of the price curve. A farm planning 1,000 fakes faces a bill above $2,000,000 before it earns a cent. Like a mountain pass that charges each extra mule more for the same trail, the fee makes a crowd too costly to hide.
